description: Four two-input logic gates, all performing the same operation, which is chosen from the right-click menu

inputs.text: One of the two inputs to the topmost gate, counted high above 1.2V and low at or below it; with nothing patched it reads 0V, which is low
The other input to the topmost gate, counted high above 1.2V and low at or below it; with nothing patched it reads 0V, which is low
The A input of that gate, counted high above 1.2V and low at or below it; with nothing patched it takes the voltage from the A jack of the gate above, and from the one above that if it is empty too
The B input of that gate, counted high above 1.2V and low at or below it; with nothing patched it takes the voltage from the B jack of the gate above, and from the one above that if it is empty too

outputs.text: The result of the chosen operation on that gate's two inputs, 10V when the result is true and 0V when it is false

notes: all four gates perform one operation together, and there is nothing on the panel that sets it: the choice is on the right-click menu, and a new module comes up as AND
the lamps across the top show which of the six operations is chosen, and each gate has a lamp for each of its two inputs and one for its output; none of them can be clicked
the table printed in the middle of the panel gives the result of all six operations for each of the four combinations of two inputs
leaving a gate's jacks empty and feeding only the topmost gate sends the same pair of signals down all four gates, which is what the normalling is for
menu: Logic Operation: AND, NAND, OR, XOR, NOR, XNOR — sets the operation all four gates perform
